title: The grinder that would not hold still
scenario:
You make short product clips for a kitchen-tools shop. A new coffee grinder launches next week. Your teammate wrote the first shot prompts, and the client sent notes on the first takes.

Use the exhibit. The move words and their meanings are from Google's video prompt guide. The shop, the prompts and the notes are made up for this case.
exhibit:
SHOT PROMPTS (made up)
  Shot 1: "Zoom toward the grinder on the counter."
  Shot 2: "Grinder hero shot rotating on the counter."
  Shot 3: "The camera shows the dial, then the beans."

CLIENT NOTES ON THE TAKES (made up)
  Shot 1: "I wanted the camera itself to come closer, past the cups."
  Shot 2: "The grinder spun around. It must stay still; the view goes around it."
  Shot 3: "Keep the camera in one place. Just look up from the dial to the beans in the hopper."
  All:    "Calm and premium. Nothing nervous."

MOVE WORDS (from Google's guide, short)
  zoom      the lens changes focal length; the camera itself doesn't move
  dolly     the camera physically moves closer or further away
  pan       the camera rotates left or right from a fixed position
  tilt      the camera rotates up or down from a fixed position
  arc shot  the camera moves in a circle or half circle around the subject
  handheld  less stable, often jerky; realism, immediacy or unease

questions.prompt: Shot 1: the client wants the camera itself to come closer. Which rewrite fits best?

options.text: Fast zoom in toward the grinder, so the picture fills up with the grinder
options.explanation: Google says a zoom changes the lens focal length and the camera itself doesn't move. The client asked for the camera to come closer.

options.text: Slow dolly in past the cups on the counter, ending close on the grinder
options.explanation: Right. Google defines a dolly as the camera physically moving closer to the subject, and the sentence names speed, start and end.

options.text: Slow pan left past the cups on the counter, ending on the grinder body
options.explanation: A pan rotates from a fixed position. The camera turns, but it does not come closer.

options.text: Static shot of the counter, then the grinder gets bigger in the frame
options.explanation: A static shot means the camera stays still. This sentence does not ask the camera to move at all.

questions.prompt: Shot 2: the grinder spun. The client wants the grinder still and the view to go around it. What is the best fix?

options.text: Keep the same words and run the shot again until the grinder stays still
options.explanation: "Rotating" allows both readings. Running it again leaves the choice to chance.

options.text: Add "faster" so the rotation looks like a deliberate, stylish product spin
options.explanation: That makes the spin stronger. The client wants the grinder not to spin at all.

options.text: Slow arc shot around the grinder, which stays still on the counter
options.explanation: Right. Google's arc shot is the camera moving around the subject, and the prompt says the grinder stays still.

options.text: Handheld shot that walks around the grinder for a more natural feel
options.explanation: Google ties handheld to jerky movement and unease. The client asked for calm, and "walks around" is less clear than an arc.

questions.prompt: Shot 3: the camera stays in one place and looks up from the dial to the beans. Which move is it?

options.text: A tilt up from the dial to the beans
options.explanation: Right. Google defines a tilt as the camera rotating up or down from a fixed position.

options.text: A pan up from the dial to the beans
options.explanation: Google defines a pan as rotating left or right, not up or down.

options.text: A dolly up from the dial to the beans
options.explanation: A dolly moves the camera closer or further away. The client wants it to stay in one place.

options.text: A truck up from the dial to the beans
options.explanation: A truck moves the camera sideways. The client wants it to stay in one place and look up.

questions.prompt: Your teammate wants one more shot: a dolly zoom on the grinder, filmed handheld. The client said calm and premium. What is your call?

options.text: Use it, because a dolly zoom is the most premium move in Google's whole list
options.explanation: Google does not rank moves as premium. It links the dolly zoom to disorientation or unease.

options.text: Use it, but write the prompt in capitals so the model takes it more seriously
options.explanation: No source here says capitals change the move. The problem is the feeling of the move, not the wording.

options.text: Use it, and add a lens flare so the shot looks more expensive and smooth
options.explanation: A lens flare does not remove the unease. Both moves still work against the brief.

options.text: Skip it: Google links both moves to unease, so use a slow, steady move
options.explanation: Right. Google says the dolly zoom often conveys disorientation or unease, and handheld can convey unease. Pick the move for its feeling.
